key_insight: The number of output tokens—rather than just model size or FLOPs—can dominate end-to-end latency in vision-language systems; reframing decoding as a multi-agent inference problem enables more efficient use of large-model decoders.
problem_solved: Addresses the bottleneck of autoregressive decoding in VLMs: varying output-token requirements cause large differences in real-world latency, so optimizing only model size or compute misses a key source of inefficiency.
method: Comprehensive latency profiling of VLM components on simulated workloads to quantify where time is spent (encoder, tokenizer, LLM decoding, I/O).
Compare different VLMs and token-output regimes to show how output length drives end-to-end latency and performance tradeoffs.
Introduce a multi-agent inference perspective (partitioned/parallelized or adaptive decoding strategies) to reduce decoding latency and better allocate token budgets across tasks.
impact: Provides practitioners with actionable evidence that decoding/token budget management is critical for deployment latency; the multi-agent inference view suggests new system and algorithm designs to speed real-world VLM applications without necessarily changing base model size.
visual_elements: Stacked-bar latency breakdown (encoder vs tokenizer vs LLM decoding) for multiple VLMs and output-token counts.
Scatter plot: output-token count vs end-to-end latency with performance contours to show tradeoffs.
Schematic diagram of multi-agent inference: multiple decoders/agents coordinating to generate tokens or adaptively stopping.
Before/after runtime comparison infographic showing latency reduction and token savings from the proposed multi-agent approach.
paper_title: Rethinking Model Efficiency: Multi-Agent Inference with Large Models
paper_authors: Sixun Dong, Juhua Hu, Steven Li, Wei Wen, Qi Qian
